content: 1. The level or effect of metoprolol can be increased by cobicistat through inhibition of hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised when these drugs are co-administered. 2. Metronidazole can elevate the level or effect of darunavir by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Cobicistat can increase the level or effect of mexiletine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 4. Darunavir can elevate the level or effect of mexiletine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended, especially when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. 5. Miconazole vaginal administration can increase the level or effect of darunavir by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 6. Cobicistat significantly increases the level or effect of midazolam (oral) by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of excessive sedation or respiratory depression. 7. Darunavir also increases the level or effect of midazolam (oral) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for serious or life-threatening events, such as prolonged sedation or respiratory depression. 8. Darunavir increases the level or effect of midazolam (intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Cobicistat increases the level or effect of midazolam (intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug, as this may prolong sedation. 10. Darunavir increases the level or effect of midostaurin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Cobicistat increases the level or effect of midostaurin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 12. Darunavir increases the level or effect of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 13. Cobicistat increases the level or effect of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust mifepristone dosage based on the patient's current regimen. 14. Mifepristone increases the level or effect of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 15. Darunavir decreases the effects of miglitol, potentially due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Both mipomersen and darunavir can increase each other's toxicity due to their potential to elevate hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 17. Darunavir increases the level or effect of mirtazapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 18. Cobicistat increases the level or effect of mirtazapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 19. Cobicistat increases the level or effect of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 20. Darunavir increases the level or effect of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are required. 21. Co-administration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with mirvetuximab soravtansine may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4, the cytotoxic component of the antibody-drug conjugate, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Monitor closely. 22. Mitotane decreases the level of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 23. Mitotane decreases the level or effect of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Darunavir increases the level or effect of modafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Cobicistat increases the level or effect of modafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Darunavir increases the level of mometasone (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 27. Cobicistat increases the level of mometasone (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, raising the risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 28. Cobicistat increases the level of mometasone (intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are required. 29. Darunavir increases the level of mometasone (intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 30. Darunavir increases the level of montelukast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 31. Nafcillin decreases the level of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 32. Nafcillin decreases the level of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Cobicistat increases the level of naldemedine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 35. Darunavir increases the level of naldemedine via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 36. Cobicistat increases the level of naldemedine via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are required. 37. Cobicistat increases the level of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of opioid withdrawal symptoms. 38. Darunavir increases the level of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of opioid withdrawal symptoms. 39. Darunavir decreases the effects of nateglinide, potentially due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 40.
